description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994, b2-22).  PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00.  Probe vs perl 5.40.3: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/expvar/{EV.pm,main.pl}
  use EV qw($Scale @List %Map get_scale set_scale);   $Scale = 2; push @List, 3; $Map{n} = 1;
  get_scale()                       perl 2         PCL 10          <-- the module does not see the importer's write
  set_scale(7); print $Scale        perl 7         PCL 2           <-- nor the importer the module's
  \$Scale == \$EV::Scale            perl aliased   PCL COPY        (\@List == \@EV::List is aliased on both)
The idiom in the wild: `use Text::Wrap qw(wrap $columns); $columns = 40;`, `use Getopt::Long; ... $opt_x`, `our $DEBUG` exported from a project's own config module and set by the script, `use vars`-era modules exporting `$VERSION`/`$Verbose`-style switches.
WHERE: the runtime's import path (`%p-do-import` and the Exporter emulation behind `use Exporter 'import'` / `use parent 'Exporter'` / `Exporter::import` / `Exporter::export`): the `@`/`%` sigils bind the SAME container object; the `$` sigil copies the VALUE into a fresh box.  perl's import is a GLOB-slot alias (`*{"caller::Scale"} = \$EV::Scale`), so both names are ONE scalar.  In PCL's global model (Direction D: a package scalar is a symbol-macro over a cell -- READ [[project_direction_d_globals]]'s facts and docs/ir-spec.md's globals section first) the fix is for the importing package's name to resolve to the EXPORTER's cell -- the same thing `*main::x = \$Other::y` must already do for a scalar glob-assignment (probe THAT first: if the explicit glob assignment aliases correctly, route the Exporter path through it -- rule 11 -- and the task is small; if it copies too, that is the real bug and this task is its most visible consequence).
CAUTION (compile-time visibility): the importing file's `$Scale` references are compiled BEFORE the module's import runs at load time (or at p-eval-always time) -- measure how an imported `@List` gets its alias today and do the same for `$`.
BAR: `cl/` (and emission if the symbol-macro target must change) => full sweep + companion lib/ + op/ legs that export scalars (`grep -a -l 'EXPORT.*\$'`), CPAN board by ROWS, guard rows in the Exporter Pl/t file (the four rows above + `local $Scale` on an imported scalar + an imported scalar inside a string eval), INVERSE-verified.


=== ROOT CAUSE LOCATED (s492b, 2026-09-21) â NOT FIXED, and it is NOT the Exporter path ===
The task's discriminating probe was taken FIRST, as it asked, and it ACQUITS the explicit glob assignment:
  package Other; our $y = 10;  *main::x = \$Other::y;  our $x;
  $x = 2  ->  $Other::y is 2;   $Other::y = 7  ->  $x is 7      IDENTICAL to perl (scratch/s492b/globalias.pl)
So `*PKG::name = \$Other::var` aliases correctly today, and routing the Exporter path through it would have changed nothing, because THAT IS ALREADY THE PATH: PCL transpiles perl's own Exporter.pm out of @INC, and its import does `*{"$callpkg\::$sym"} = \${"$pkg\::$sym"}`.  (`p-import-perl-symbol`, the runtime's own -copy convenience, is NOT reached for an Exporter module â instrumented and measured: it never fires for `use EV qw($Scale)`.)

THE BUG IS ONE STEP EARLIER, in the SYMBOLIC half of the backslash (scratch/s492b/symref.pl, sref3.pl):
  our $g = 7;
  my $hard = \$g;            $$hard = 5;   ->  $g is 5    RIGHT (and \$$r through a hard ref is right too)
  my $sym  = \${"main::g"};  $$sym  = 9;   ->  $g is 7    WRONG (perl: 9)
  my $n = "main::g"; \${$n}                             same, WRONG
  \${"EV2::Scale"} == \$EV2::Scale                      DIFF (perl: same)
Exporter builds every scalar export with exactly that spelling, so the importer gets a reference to a COPY and the two names are separate boxes from the first moment (probed before any write: `\$Scale == \$EV::Scale` is COPY).  @ and % exports alias because their VALUE *is* the container: `p-cast-@`/`p-cast-%` answer with the live vector / hash-table (`%p-symref-array` / `%p-symref-hash`), while `p-cast-$`'s string arm answers with `%p-symref-scalar-value` â the VALUE, not the box â and `p-backslash` then wraps a raw value in a FRESH box.

EMISSION (measured): `\${"main::g"}` is `(p-backslash (p-cast-$ "main::g" (p-symref-site)))`, byte for byte the same shape as the hard-ref `\$$r` = `(p-backslash (p-cast-$ $r))`.  So the difference is entirely inside `p-cast-$`'s two arms.

TWO CANDIDATE FIX SHAPES (neither taken here; the batch had no budget left for an emission change plus its bar):
  (1) RUNTIME-ONLY: give the symbolic arm a REF-CONTEXT twin.  `%p-symref-box` already exists (it is what `%p-symref-scalar-set` writes through) and already vivifies on the setf side.  `p-cast-$` cannot simply return the box â its contract is the READ value, and every rvalue `${"name"}` would change shape â so the ref site needs its own entry point.
  (2) EMISSION: lower `\${EXPR}` to a form that asks for the PLACE (`(p-backslash-symref EXPR site)`) which resolves to `%p-symref-box` for a string and falls back to today's behaviour for a hard ref.  The operand's kind is only known at run time, so the dispatch stays in the runtime either way; what the emission buys is that ONLY the backslash site changes, leaving every read alone.  Shape (2) is the one to cost first.
BREAKING CASES TO PROBE WITH EITHER: `\${"5"}` and the capture family (read-only â `%p-symref-read-only-p` must still die), `\${"nosuchvar"}` (perl vivifies), a magic name the runtime stores UNBOXED (`%p-symref-symbol-value`'s arm â there is no box to return), `local $Imported`, an imported scalar inside a string eval, and the compile-time-visibility caution already in this task.


=== DONE (s495f, 2026-09-25) -- SHAPE (2) ===
EMISSION: Pl/ExprToCL.pm `_backslash_of` -- the `\` of a `(p-cast-$ EXPR [SITE])` form lowers to `(p-backslash-cast-$ EXPR [SITE])`; every other `\` stays `(p-backslash X)` and every rvalue `${…}` stays p-cast-$.  corpus-diff vs 3d9b3712: exactly ref.t, postfixderef.t, sort.t change -- each at a `\${…}` site, nothing else.
RUNTIME: p-backslash-cast-$ -- a SYMBOLIC name answers a ref to the package CELL (%p-symref-cell: vivified like a `${"name"} = …` write; NIL -- i.e. today's copy -- for the read-only capture family, the computed $&-family and magics stored raw); a HARD scalar ref answers a ref to its REFERENT (%p-scalar-ref-referent), so `\${$r} == $r` and `\${\$v}` writes $v (both copied before, pre-existing); anything else (a non-scalar referent -> p-cast-$'s fatal) keeps (p-backslash (p-cast-$ …)).  The operand is read from the box's RAW slot, so a tied operand is FETCHed once, by the fallback.
PROBES vs perl (scratch/s495f/p-symref.pl 17 lines, p-symref2.pl 9, p-exp.pl 9 incl. the task's four EV rows, `local $Imported`, string-eval read AND write, BEGIN visibility): identical except `\${"1"}` then `$$r = 2` (perl dies read-only, PCL writes -- PRE-EXISTING on 3d9b3712, the #873 family).  BREAKING list: \${"5"} keeps the value copy (read-only family), \${"nosuch"} vivifies (same as \$main::nosuch), \${"0"} / \${"&"} unchanged, `local` on the aliased cell = perl's glob-slot local, eval q{} sees the alias.
BAR: full sweep GATE clean TOTAL 18686 (+0) -- ref.t / postfixderef.t / sort.t results identical; guard rows Pl/t/ref-to-ref-01.t 46-47, inverse-verified; everyday programs/exporter-tags-lib -> same.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing): an EXPORTED SCALAR is imported as a COPY, not an alias -- `use EV qw($Scale); $Scale = 2;` does not change `$EV::Scale` (the module keeps seeing 10), and a later change by the module never reaches the importer; exported ARRAYS and HASHES are aliased correctly
